sourcedFrom: Wilson Combat Owner's Manual For AR9 (9mm carbine) — Copyright 2019 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. (2019)
cleanIntro:
The AR9 is Wilson Combat's 9mm carbine on AR-pattern receivers. It looks like an AR-15 but it does not strip like one: Wilson's field strip leaves the buffer and recoil spring in the stock, and the bolt assembly comes out as one piece without a cam pin to pull.

Two things to carry through every step. The AR9 has no magazine disconnect, so it will fire with the magazine out — an empty magwell is not an empty rifle. And the trigger is a drop-in unit (Wilson calls it the TTU) with a permanent dry-film lubricant: brush it, never put it in an ultrasonic cleaner, and do not oil it beyond a very light coat of rust preventative.

Wilson's book takes the bolt apart as far as the extractor, leaves the ejector in, and shows how to drop the trigger unit out of the lower. The handguard is armorer information only and is not part of normal maintenance.

steps.title: Muzzle safe, finger off, selector on SAFE
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction, keep your finger out of the trigger guard, and rotate the thumb safety to SAFE. The safety lever is on the left side of the lower receiver; SAFE blocks the trigger.
steps.prose: Everything that follows assumes these three. If the selector will not go to SAFE, carry on unloading and set it once the rifle is clear.
steps.quote: Make sure the firearm is pointed in a safe direction, your finger is away from the trigger and the thumb safety is in the SAFE position.
steps.cite: Wilson Combat Owner's Manual For AR9 (9mm carbine) — Copyright 2019 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Firing & Unloading, printed p.35

steps.title: ⚠ Magazine out — it fires without one
steps.action: Press the magazine release with your index finger and take the magazine out of the magwell. Removing the magazine does not make the AR9 safe: there is no magazine disconnect, so a round in the chamber will still fire.
steps.prose: The magazine coming out only stops the next round feeding. The chamber is the next step.
steps.caution: This firearm does not have a magazine disconnect. Firearm will fire without a magazine.
steps.quote: To release a magazine from the firearm, depress the magazine release with your index finger.
steps.cite: Wilson Combat Owner's Manual For AR9 (9mm carbine) — Copyright 2019 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Operation Controls — Magazine Catch, printed p.30

steps.title: Charging handle fully back, lock the bolt open
steps.action: Pull the charging handle all the way to the rear and lock the bolt open: hold the handle back and press the bottom of the bolt release, then let the handle forward until the bolt rests on the bolt catch. Any chambered round is extracted on the way back.
steps.prose: Keep your face and hand clear of the ejection port while the round comes out.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine, retract the charging handle fully to the rear and manually lock the bolt open.
steps.cite: Wilson Combat Owner's Manual For AR9 (9mm carbine) — Copyright 2019 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Firing & Unloading, printed p.35

steps.title: LOOK into the chamber and the magwell
steps.action: With the bolt locked open, look through the ejection port into the chamber and down into the magazine well. Only when you have seen both empty is the rifle unloaded.
steps.prose: Cycling the action is not the check. Seeing an empty chamber is.
steps.quote: Visually inspect the chamber to make sure the firearm is not loaded.
steps.cite: Wilson Combat Owner's Manual For AR9 (9mm carbine) — Copyright 2019 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Firing & Unloading, printed p.35

steps.title: Close the bolt on the empty chamber
steps.action: Press the bolt release button and let the bolt go forward. Wilson's field strip starts with the bolt closed.
steps.prose: Only close it once you have seen the chamber empty in the step before.
steps.quote: Close the bolt by pushing the bolt release button.
steps.cite: Wilson Combat Owner's Manual For AR9 (9mm carbine) — Copyright 2019 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Field Stripping, printed p.36

steps.title: Rear takedown pin — push LEFT to RIGHT until it stops
steps.action: Push the rear takedown pin across from the left side to the right until it stops. It stays captive in the lower. On some rifles it is tight enough to need a punch and a hammer to start it.
steps.prose: Stop when it stops. It is held by a detent and is not meant to come out of the receiver.
steps.quote: Push the rear takedown pin from left to right until it stops (the rear takedown pin may fit so tightly in some firearms that a punch and hammer is needed to move it).
steps.cite: Wilson Combat Owner's Manual For AR9 (9mm carbine) — Copyright 2019 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Field Stripping, printed p.36

steps.title: Pivot the upper and lower apart
steps.action: Swing the receivers apart on the front pivot pin. The upper stays hinged to the lower; Wilson's field strip does not push the pivot pin out.
steps.prose: With the rear open you have room to get the bolt out the back of the upper.
steps.quote: Pivot the upper and lower receiver apart.
steps.cite: Wilson Combat Owner's Manual For AR9 (9mm carbine) — Copyright 2019 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Field Stripping, printed p.36

steps.title: Charging handle and bolt halfway back
steps.action: Draw the charging handle back, bringing the bolt assembly with it, about halfway to the rear.
steps.prose: Halfway is enough to get a grip on the bolt assembly at the rear of the upper.
steps.quote: Retract the charging handle and bolt assembly about 1/2 way to the rear.
steps.cite: Wilson Combat Owner's Manual For AR9 (9mm carbine) — Copyright 2019 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Field Stripping, printed p.37

steps.title: Bolt assembly out
steps.action: Slide the bolt assembly out of the back of the upper receiver and set it on the bench in one piece.
steps.prose: The bolt assembly is cleaned as a unit after every range trip; taking it apart is in DEEP CLEAN.
steps.cite: Wilson Combat Owner's Manual For AR9 (9mm carbine) — Copyright 2019 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Field Stripping, printed p.37

steps.title: Charging handle back until it stops, then DOWN and out
steps.action: Pull the charging handle the rest of the way back until it stops, then push it downward and lift it out of the upper receiver.
steps.prose: It only drops out at the end of its travel. Do not lever it out anywhere else.
steps.quote: Retract the charging handle to the rear until it stops, then push it downward and remove from the upper receiver.
steps.cite: Wilson Combat Owner's Manual For AR9 (9mm carbine) — Copyright 2019 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Field Stripping, printed p.37

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: On the bench: the upper and lower receivers, still hinged on the pivot pin, the bolt assembly, and the charging handle. That is Wilson's field strip. The handguard stays on. Wilson's book goes on to take the bolt apart down to the extractor and to drop the trigger unit out of the lower — that is in DEEP CLEAN.
steps.prose: Nothing else comes off for routine cleaning.
steps.quote: Normal field stripping and maintenance of the firearm does not require removal of the handguard.
steps.cite: Wilson Combat Owner's Manual For AR9 (9mm carbine) — Copyright 2019 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Wilson Combat Handguard Removal, printed p.50

deepSteps.title: Firing pin retaining pin out — left side
deepSteps.action: Pull the firing pin retaining pin out of the bolt assembly. It sits at the left-centre of the bolt assembly.
deepSteps.prose: Wilson asks for a thorough bolt cleaning to be done with the bolt taken apart, starting here.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the firing pin retaining pin at the left/center of the bolt assembly.
deepSteps.cite: Wilson Combat Owner's Manual For AR9 (9mm carbine) — Copyright 2019 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Bolt Assembly Cleaning, printed p.38

deepSteps.title: Firing pin and its spring out
deepSteps.action: Take the firing pin and its spring out of the bolt assembly. Keep the spring with the pin.
deepSteps.prose: If the pin will not come, the retaining pin is still in.
deepSteps.cite: Wilson Combat Owner's Manual For AR9 (9mm carbine) — Copyright 2019 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Bolt Assembly Cleaning, printed p.38

deepSteps.title: Extractor pin: push in on the RIGHT, pull out on the LEFT
deepSteps.action: Push the extractor pin in from the right side of the bolt and draw it out on the left side, then lift the extractor off the bolt. Before anything moves, look at how the extractor, its spring and its O-ring sit — they go back the same way.
deepSteps.prose: The extractor spring pushes on the extractor; keep a thumb over it so the small parts do not leave the bench.
deepSteps.quote: (a) Push the extractor pin in on the right side of the bolt and pull extractor pin out on the left side of the bolt, (b) then remove the extractor from the bolt. Note the relationship of the internal parts.
deepSteps.cite: Wilson Combat Owner's Manual For AR9 (9mm carbine) — Copyright 2019 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Bolt Assembly Cleaning, printed p.38

deepSteps.title: Leave the ejector in
deepSteps.action: Do not take the ejector out for normal cleaning. Only if it becomes sticky or frozen does Wilson have you drive out its roll pin, clean it, and reinstall it with a new standard AR-15 ejector pin; an AR-15 ejector removal tool helps.
deepSteps.prose: A free-moving ejector needs nothing more than cleaning and oil in place.
deepSteps.quote: It is not recommended to remove your AR9 ejector during normal maintenance.
deepSteps.cite: Wilson Combat Owner's Manual For AR9 (9mm carbine) — Copyright 2019 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Bolt Assembly Cleaning, printed p.38

deepSteps.title: Trigger unit: upper off, SAFE, chamber checked
deepSteps.action: To take the trigger unit out, first set the selector to SAFE, take the magazine out and look into the chamber, then take the upper receiver off the lower.
deepSteps.prose: The trigger unit comes out of the lower on its own; the upper has to be clear of it.
deepSteps.quote: Set firearm to SAFE (a), remove magazine and visually verify that the chamber is empty.
deepSteps.cite: Wilson Combat Owner's Manual For AR9 (9mm carbine) — Copyright 2019 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Removing Tactical Trigger Unit (TTU), printed p.44

deepSteps.title: Drive out the hammer pivot pin
deepSteps.action: With a punch, drive the hammer pivot pin out of the lower receiver.
deepSteps.prose: Support the lower so the punch does not mark the receiver.
deepSteps.quote: Using a punch, drive out the hammer pivot pin from the receiver.
deepSteps.cite: Wilson Combat Owner's Manual For AR9 (9mm carbine) — Copyright 2019 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Removing Tactical Trigger Unit (TTU), printed p.44

deepSteps.title: Drive out the trigger pivot pin, lift the unit out
deepSteps.action: With a punch, drive the trigger pivot pin out of the receiver and lift the trigger unit out of the lower. If it will not come out, set the selector to FIRE. If it still will not come, loosen the pistol grip screw part-way until the safety selector can come out of the receiver; once the trigger unit is out, put the selector back and tighten the pistol grip screw.
deepSteps.prose: The selector can trap the unit. Moving or removing the selector is the cure, not force.
deepSteps.caution: If the trigger assembly cannot be removed set selector to FIRE (b).
deepSteps.quote: Using a punch, drive out the trigger pivot pin from the receiver.
deepSteps.cite: Wilson Combat Owner's Manual For AR9 (9mm carbine) — Copyright 2019 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Removing Tactical Trigger Unit (TTU), printed p.44

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Trigger unit: never in an ultrasonic cleaner
deepSteps.action: The trigger unit carries a permanent dry-film lubricant. Clean it with a nylon brush and solvent and dry it with compressed air — never in an ultrasonic cleaner. This is where Wilson's book stops taking the rifle apart.
deepSteps.prose: The dry-film coating is the reason: the unit is brushed and blown dry, not bathed.
deepSteps.quote: The TTU has a permanent dry-film lubricant applied so do not clean in an ultrasonic cleaner.
deepSteps.cite: Wilson Combat Owner's Manual For AR9 (9mm carbine) — Copyright 2019 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — TTU Cleaning Maintenance, printed p.47

cleaning.name: BOLT ASSEMBLY
tasks: After every range trip: soak the bolt in carbon remover, then wipe or brush every interior area clean of powder fouling, corrosion and dirt.
Clean the extractor and the extractor pocket thoroughly.
Clean the outside of every part and the inside of the bolt assembly; a bolt cleaning tool may be needed to get all the carbon off.
Do not use a tool that will mark or deeply scratch the bolt's finish.
Oil every outside surface of the bolt when finished — the four contact rails, the extractor and the ejector.

cleaning.name: BORE AND CHAMBER
tasks: Run a tight patch soaked in bore cleaner through the bore and let it soak 5 to 15 minutes.
Bronze bore brush through the bore six times; a bore guide is recommended.
Another soaked patch, then dry patches until they come out clean.
Clean the chamber with the bore.
Do not use lubricants Wilson has not authorised on this rifle.
Going into storage: an oiled patch through the bore, then a dry one.

cleaning.name: UPPER RECEIVER AND CHARGING HANDLE
tasks: Clean the inside of the upper receiver with carbon remover or bore cleaner.
Lightly oil the bearing surfaces of the charging handle.

cleaning.name: LOWER AND TRIGGER UNIT (TTU)
tasks: Brush the trigger unit clean with a nylon brush and solvent, then dry it with compressed air.
⛔ Never clean the trigger unit in an ultrasonic cleaner — it carries a permanent dry-film lubricant.
No oil on the trigger unit beyond a very light coat of rust preventative.

reassembly: Extractor and extractor spring back into the pocket in the bolt, secured with the extractor pin. A non-marring vice to hold the bolt helps.
Firing pin and firing pin spring back in, secured with the firing pin retainer. The retainer must sit flush with the bolt assembly so it does not drag on the receiver.

If the trigger unit was out: set it half-cocked with its spring leg resting on the cross pin, selector on FIRE, lower it in with the trigger passing into the trigger guard, and tip its tail down under the selector.

Trigger pin, then hammer pin, each offset groove first, from the left side; push down on the hammer face to get the hammer pin in. Tap both flush on both sides — if a pin pushes back out, start the pins again.
Charging handle halfway into the upper receiver.
Bolt assembly into the upper with its key riding inside the charging handle.
Push the bolt assembly and charging handle fully forward together.
Pivot the upper back onto the lower and push the takedown pin from right to left until it is flush.
Run the function check before any live ammunition.
fncheck: Unloaded, magazine out, chamber seen empty. Selector on SAFE, pull the charging handle back and let it go, then pull the trigger: the hammer must NOT fall. Selector on FIRE, pull the trigger: the hammer must fall with a snap. Hold the trigger back and cycle the charging handle, then let the trigger out slowly: you should hear a click and the hammer must not fall. Pull the trigger again: the hammer must fall. Wilson has the hold-and-reset part repeated five times. If the rifle fails any part of this, do not use it and contact Wilson Combat.
